sections.title: Edit
sections.body: Adjust tone and color on the selected photo using Edit. These settings develop a rendered result while the original photo stays in its own file; export a new image when ready.

sections.title: Crop
sections.body: Change the image boundary and straightening in Crop. Check the full image before committing a tight crop; the original remains available.

sections.title: Remove
sections.body: Use Remove for local distractions. Inspect the repaired area at a useful zoom and undo an unwanted result rather than repeatedly painting over it.

sections.title: Masking
sections.body: Limit adjustments to a local region with Masking. Use the mask overlay to inspect the affected region before changing tone or color.

sections.title: Red Eye
sections.body: Use Red Eye for the red reflection in eyes. Work closely enough to position the correction over the pupil and inspect both eyes afterward.

sections.title: Versions
sections.body: Use Versions to compare saved edit alternatives for a photo. Keep your library backup and original media; versions do not replace those backups.

sections.title: Keywords and Info
sections.body: Use Keywords to organize search terms, and Info to inspect photo metadata. Library labels organize photos without renaming your original image files.

sections.title: Compare, Survey and Reference
sections.body: Compare places two photos together, Survey tiles the selection, and Reference keeps one photo beside the active edit. These are viewing aids; they do not export a composite image.

sections.title: Before and after
sections.body: Compare the original and edited render in a before/after view. Return to the normal edit view before judging the final exported framing.

sections.title: Select and transform
sections.body: Use Select to choose objects on a slide. Drag a selected object to move it; use its handles to resize or rotate. Check which object is selected before deleting or formatting.

sections.title: Preset shapes
sections.body: Choose a shape preset and draw it on the slide. Adjust size, fill and outline after insertion. Use text boxes for independent text rather than drawing individual letters.

sections.title: Text boxes
sections.body: Create a text box to add editable slide text. Enter text, then leave text editing to move or resize the whole box. A text caret and an object selection act on different things.

sections.title: Pen, highlighter and eraser
sections.body: Use Ink pen or highlighter to draw strokes; use the ink eraser to remove strokes. These are slide objects, so inspect the result in slideshow view before presenting.

sections.title: Edit points
sections.body: Use Edit Points on a suitable shape to adjust vertices and curve handles. Keep a copy before extensive path edits, and undo if the outline stops matching your intent.

sections.title: Tables
sections.body: Drag table column or row boundaries to change their size. Edit cell text separately; resizing a table is different from scaling a screenshot of it.

sections.title: Home
sections.body: Use Home for text and paragraph formatting. Select existing text before applying a change; with only a caret, some formatting affects new text instead.

sections.title: Insert
sections.body: Use Insert to add document objects such as tables, pictures and other supported content. Select the inserted object to reveal its contextual formatting controls.

sections.title: Draw
sections.body: Use Draw for ink marks rather than ordinary typed paragraphs. Keep important text as editable text when it needs search, copying or later revision.

sections.title: Design and Layout
sections.body: Design controls document styling; Layout controls page geometry such as margins, orientation and columns. Check all affected pages before exporting.

sections.title: References
sections.body: Use References for supported document references and navigation structures. Update generated content after editing headings or source information.

sections.title: Mailings
sections.body: Use Mailings for supported merge workflows. Check the source data and preview records before producing final copies; keep a separate editable master.

sections.title: Review
sections.body: Use Review to inspect proofing, comments and revisions. Review proposed changes individually when meaning matters; spell checking does not establish factual correctness.

sections.title: View
sections.body: Change the document view and visible navigation controls in View. Reading settings change how you view the document; page layout still determines its printed result.

sections.title: Developer and Zotero
sections.body: Developer and Zotero expose specialist controls and integrations. External integrations may need their own installation or setup; an inactive control does not indicate that its dependency is bundled.

sections.title: Contextual formatting
sections.body: Selecting a table, picture, shape, equation, chart or SmartArt object exposes its relevant contextual tab. Return to the text caret for ordinary text editing.

sections.title: Home
sections.body: Use Home to format selected cells and manage routine editing. Confirm the active range before pasting, clearing or changing number formats.

sections.title: Insert
sections.body: Use Insert for supported tables, charts and objects. Select the source cells first where a chart or table needs data; inspect labels and series afterward.

sections.title: Draw
sections.body: Use Draw for ink or drawn annotations. Drawing over cells does not change the values or formulas stored in those cells.

sections.title: Page Layout
sections.body: Set printed page arrangement in Page Layout. Check scaling, margins and print area before producing a PDF or printed copy.

sections.title: Formulas
sections.body: Enter formulas in cells and use Formulas for function-related controls. Check references and error values; formatting a number changes its appearance, not its stored calculation.

sections.title: Data
sections.body: Use Data for supported sorting, filtering and data operations. Select the whole related table before sorting so columns stay aligned. Keep an original before destructive transformations.

sections.title: Review
sections.body: Use Review for document review controls. Check comments and protected ranges before sharing an editable workbook.

sections.title: View
sections.body: Use View to change workbook presentation and navigation. A hidden row, column or sheet may still contain data used by formulas.

sections.title: Automate
sections.body: Use Automate for supported automation controls. Inspect an automation before running it, and preserve a workbook copy because automated actions may affect many cells.

sections.title: Draw
sections.body: Use Draw to create geometric entities. Establish drawing units and precision before detailed work, and confirm coordinates or object snaps instead of estimating critical geometry.

sections.title: Modify
sections.body: Use Modify to change existing geometry. Select only the intended entities before moving, trimming, extending or transforming them; inspect the result at intersections.

sections.title: Dimension
sections.body: Use Dimension to annotate measured geometry. Check drawing units, dimension style and scale; displayed precision should match the intended design tolerance.

sections.title: Format
sections.body: Use Format for drawing presentation such as layers and styles. Organize related geometry on appropriate layers so visibility and plotting can be controlled together.

sections.title: Insert
sections.body: Use Insert for supported drawing content and references. Confirm the incoming scale and insertion point before combining drawings from different sources.

sections.title: View and Window
sections.body: Use View for navigation and display controls, and Window for open drawing organization. Save drawing files separately; changing a viewport does not create a new saved drawing.

sections.title: Tools
sections.body: Tools contains specialist drawing and configuration commands. Read the command prompt and confirm options rather than assuming a command has completed after the first click.

sections.title: New graph
sections.body: Create a graph for a procedural material. Nodes compute outputs from their inputs; connect compatible sockets to build a result rather than expecting an unconnected node to affect the preview.

sections.title: Open package
sections.body: Open a saved material package to continue editing. Keep linked resources with the package and inspect missing inputs before exporting outputs.

sections.title: Save
sections.body: Save the editable package with its graph structure. Saving a package is separate from exporting rendered material maps.

sections.title: Undo and Redo
sections.body: Undo the latest reversible graph edit, or Redo an undone edit. Keep a saved package copy before a major graph restructuring.

sections.title: Export outputs
sections.body: Export the graph outputs as material maps for another application. Check map names, output dimensions and the expected color space in the receiving application.

sections.title: Compute status and preview size
sections.body: The status bar reports computation and preview size. A reduced preview helps iteration but is not proof of final output quality; inspect the exported maps at their intended resolution.

sections.title: Export a PDF
sections.body: Export a PDF to a supported editable, image or text format. Choose the output appropriate to the receiving app; conversion may change layout, fonts or interactive content. Some export formats are still planned.

sections.title: Fill & Sign
sections.body: Add text, marks, dates, initials or a signature appearance to a form. A drawn signature appearance is separate from cryptographically signing with a certificate.

sections.title: Edit a PDF
sections.body: This tool family is still marked planned in the source. Do not rely on general PDF content editing being complete. Use the original authoring document for unsupported changes.

sections.title: Create a PDF
sections.body: Create a new PDF from supported input. Check page dimensions, orientation and font appearance in the resulting PDF before sharing it.

sections.title: Combine files
sections.body: Combine supported files into one PDF. Review their order and page orientation, then save to a new destination rather than overwriting the input files.

sections.title: Organize pages
sections.body: Use the page overview to arrange, rotate, insert, extract or remove supported pages. Review the resulting page order and keep an original before deleting pages.

sections.title: Add comments
sections.body: Add review comments and annotations. These communicate proposed changes; they do not necessarily modify the underlying page content.

sections.title: Scan & OCR
sections.body: Use the available scan and OCR controls to bring image content into a searchable workflow. OCR can misread text; inspect names, numbers and exported text.

sections.title: Protect a PDF
sections.body: This tool family is still marked planned in the source. Do not assume a document has encryption or access restrictions merely because this panel is visible.

sections.title: Redact a PDF
sections.body: Use the dedicated redaction workflow for sensitive content. A black drawing or annotation is not a substitute for applied redaction. Retain a private original and inspect the sanitized copy before sharing.

sections.title: Compress a PDF
sections.body: Create a smaller PDF using supported compression options. Inspect small text and images afterward, especially when preparing a print document.

sections.title: Prepare a form
sections.body: Create and arrange supported form fields, then test their values and tab order. Save the editable form separately from a completed or flattened copy.

sections.title: Add a stamp
sections.body: Add a stamp annotation to the document. Stamps are visual marks; they do not by themselves prove authorship or certificate validity.

sections.title: Use a certificate
sections.body: Use the supported certificate controls for digital-signature workflows. Manage certificate credentials privately; signature trust and the validity of document content are separate questions.

sections.title: Use print production
sections.body: This tool family is still marked planned in the source. Do not treat the available UI as evidence of complete professional prepress validation.

sections.title: Measure objects
sections.body: Measure supported objects on a PDF page. Set and confirm the scale first; measuring a scan without a known scale does not establish real-world dimensions.

sections.title: Compare files
sections.body: Compare two PDF versions to inspect differences. Review the actual changed pages; a comparison result does not establish that every semantic difference was detected.

sections.title: Use guided actions
sections.body: Use guided actions for supported multi-step processing. Check input and output locations and keep originals before running a batch.

sections.title: Prepare for accessibility
sections.body: Inspect and prepare supported accessibility structures. Machine checks alone do not establish accessible reading order or usable alternative text; review the document with its intended reading workflow.

sections.title: Apply PDF standards
sections.body: Use supported PDF standards checks or conversion controls. Confirm the requested profile and read reported limitations before describing the output as conforming.

sections.title: Add search index
sections.body: This tool family is still marked planned in the source. Basic document search and a generated multi-document search index are different capabilities.

sections.title: Use JavaScript
sections.body: This tool family is still marked planned in the source. Do not assume PDF scripts or scripted form behavior will run as they do in another PDF application.

sections.title: AI assistant
sections.body: The AI assistant requires an optional provider. This is not a bundled unlimited AI service; provider availability and setup determine which actions can run.
